task.description:
Run the FULL project test suite on `feature/WF03-ISS0179-20260821` (already checked out) before this branch merges. The change under test (`test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs`'s advisory-lock serialization) already passed its own module's tests (10/10, independently re-run twice) and idiom review -- this step is the full-suite regression check the merge step will otherwise be trusting blind.

Use `sh scripts/test_parallel.sh` per this project's standard full-suite mechanism, with `TEST_PARALLEL_N=4` on this host (the default nproc-based N is known to saturate the shared Postgres pool at `mix ecto.create` time on this specific 16-core host -- ISS-0212/ISS-0194 already cover this, no need to re-derive it, just use the override).

ATTRIBUTE EVERY FAILURE STRUCTURALLY, per `core-directives.md`'s 'Failure Attribution Is Structural, Never By Count-Matching' -- this suite carries a standing set of pre-existing failures and 'green' means no failure attributable to this branch, not zero failures. For each failure: is the failing module or its dependencies in `git diff --name-only main...feature/WF03-ISS0179-20260821`? The only file this branch changes is `test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs` -- if a failure is in that module, it needs a genuine causal argument (not just presence), since it is exactly the module this run just changed.

Write the test report per this project's convention (`test/reports/`) and record it in `artifacts_out`.
acceptance_criteria: The full suite was actually run via TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 sh scripts/test_parallel.sh and real pass/fail counts are quoted
Every failure is attributed structurally, never by count-matching against a prior run
Any failure in test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs specifically is checked for a genuine causal connection to this run's own change, not cleared by assumption
A test report is written to test/reports/ and listed in artifacts_out

result.summary: Ran the full suite via TEST_PARALLEL_N=4 sh scripts/test_parallel.sh (per this run's handoff instruction, no re-derivation needed). All 4 partitions completed cleanly with no crashes: combined 1289 tests, 5 properties, 2 failures (1292/1294 passed). Both failures are one group (Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest, test/mix/tasks/letflow_check_test_test.exs, lines 105 and 126), attributed structurally: Route 1 -- neither that file nor lib/mix/tasks/letflow.check.test.ex appears in `git diff --name-only main...feature/WF03-ISS0179-20260821` (which contains only handoffs, one design doc, and test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs, the one file this branch changes); Route 3 -- the symptom pair (a 60000ms ExUnit.TimeoutError at collect/2, and a real subprocess 'exited 1' Mix.Error where a substring-match message was expected) and root cause (install_fake_mix/2's fake-mix fixture is POSIX-only: an extensionless `#!/sh` file plus ':' PATH-prepend, neither of which Windows resolves, so run/1 shells out to the REAL mix and recurses) exactly match docs/issues/ISS-0107.yaml (open, MAJOR, filed 2026-08-20, same file, same mechanism, same two symptom shapes). Also directly reproduced ISS-0107's documented orphaned-process side effect on this host during this step: after the run, one erl.exe (PID 14552) was still running with command line `erl.exe ... -extra "...\mix" test` -- the timed-out test's nested `mix test` child, never killed by the outer 60000ms timeout. Killed via Stop-Process; confirmed gone. test/letflow/identity_migration_test.exs (this branch's one changed file) ran inside partition 4 and is clean: 257 tests, 0 failures, exit 0 -- confirmed via `grep -n IdentityMigrationTest partition-*.log`, only matching partition 4. No failure is attributable to this branch's change. PASS.
result.next_action: Route to ORCH / WF-04 Step 1 (RELEASE-VALIDATOR) -- PASS, no failure attributable to this branch. RELEASE-VALIDATOR re-runs the suite independently. Flag: the two Mix.Tasks.Letflow.Check.TestTest failures are the already-open, Windows-specific ISS-0107, which also leaves an orphaned nested `mix test` erl.exe process on timeout -- check for stray erl.exe processes after any run hitting this same failure pair on a Windows host.
